events.description: 4. ORDER: Upon review of the Complaint, the Court finds that this case is substantially related to a previously filed case, Berry III v. Ashcroft, et al., No. 4:22-cv-465, which was originally assigned to the Honorable John A. Ross. To maintain the random assignment of cases pursuant to Local Rule 2.08(A), and under the authority of 28 U.S.C. § 137(a), the undersigned directs the Clerk of Court to reassign this case to the Honorable John A. Ross. Signed by Chief District Judge Stephen R. Clark on 9/4/2026. (KXS) (Entered: 09/04/2026)

evidence.document: The docket as the RECAP Archive holds it

events.description: 5. ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE: IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that Plaintiff Paul Berry III must show cause in writing no later than 12:00 p.m. CT on September 7, 2026 as to why his requests to convene a three-judge panel and obtain the equitable relief he seeks should not be denied in light of the procedural impossibility of complying with 28 U.S.C. § 2284(b)(2). Plaintiff is advised that he must respond to this order before the Court will entertain any further request for relief. (Show Cause Response due by 9/7/2026.) Signed by Sr. District Judge John A. Ross on 9/4/2026. (KXS) (Entered: 09/04/2026)

events.description: 7. ORDER: Ultimately, this Court cannot determine a proper path forward until the United States Supreme Court has ruled on Missouri's application for a stay of von Glahn. The Court therefore finds it necessary and appropriate to hold Plaintiff's requests for emergency relief in abeyance pending such a ruling. The Court will determine next steps as appropriate after that ruling. SEE ORDER FOR DETAILS. Signed by Sr. District Judge John A. Ross on 9/8/2026. (CLT) (Entered: 09/08/2026)

events.description: 39. ORDER: IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that Defendants' motion to stay the case until after the November 3, 2026, election is GRANTED. (Doc. 24 ). Defendants shall file a Rule 12 responsive pleading by December 4, 2026. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that Plaintiff's motion to withdraw (Doc. 29) his original motion for temporary restraining order (Doc. 18 ) is GRANTED. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that Plaintiff's motions to waive the page limitation (Doc. 32) and to respond out of time (Doc. 37 ) are GRANTED. IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the following motions are DENIED: 1. Motion to set aside abeyance (Doc. 10). 2. Motion to shorten time (Doc. 21). 3. Motion for temporary restraining order (Doc. 30). 4. Motion for hearing (Doc. 33). 5. Motion to shorten time (Doc. 34) 6. Motion for trial date (Doc. 36). SEE ORDER FOR DETAILS. ( Response to Court due by 12/4/2026.) Signed by Sr. District Judge John A. Ross on 9/25/2026. (CLT) (Entered: 09/25/2026)

events.description: 47. ORDER: This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff's motion for review (Doc. 42) and motion for reconsideration (Doc. 43) challenging the Court's denial of emergency relief. Upon review of the motions, the Court finds no basis to grant the Plaintiff requests, particularly in light of the Eighth Circuit's judgment denying Plaintiff's writ petition in this case and the United States Supreme Court's per curiam decision in People Not Politicians, et al. v. Robert Onder, et al., No 26A388, 609 U.S. --- (2026). Accordingly, IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that Plaintiff's motions are DENIED. (Doc. 42, 43). Signed by Sr. District Judge John A. Ross on 9/28/2026. (CLT) (Entered: 09/28/2026)
